sn36.5:1.3: Pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
sn36.5:1.4: Pleasant feeling, bhikkhus, should be seen as painful; painful feeling should be seen as a dart; neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling should be seen as impermanent.
sn36.5:1.5: “When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has seen pleasant feeling as painful, painful feeling as a dart, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling as impermanent,
sn36.5:1.6: he is called a bhikkhu who sees rightly. He has cut off craving, severed the fetters, and by completely breaking through conceit, he has made an end to suffering.”
sn36.5:2.1: One who has seen the pleasant as painful
sn36.5:2.2: And the painful as a dart,
sn36.5:2.3:
Seen as impermanent the peaceful feeling
Neither painful nor pleasant:
sn36.5:3.1: He is a bhikkhu who sees rightly,
sn36.5:3.4: He is taintless in this very life.
sn36.5:3.6:
with the body’s breakup
The knowledge-master cannot be reckoned.
